steps.title: Import Vue and ref
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a module
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have Vue and ref available to use in your component.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and ref.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import Vue and ref from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create MouseTracker component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named MouseTracker with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Define a component using the defineComponent function from Vue. The setup function should return an empty object for now.
steps.seedCode:
import { defineComponent, ref } from 'vue'

// Create MouseTracker component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A MouseTracker component is defined with a setup function that returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The MouseTracker component is defined using defineComponent and has a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the MouseTracker component with a setup function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using defineComponent and have a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you're using defineComponent and have a setup function that returns an empty object.

steps.title: Initialize mouse position state
steps.instruction: Inside the MouseTracker component, use ref to create two reactive variables named x and y, both initialized to 0.
steps.hint: You'll need to call ref(0) twice to create separate reactive references for x and y coordinates.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have reactive x and y variables ready to track mouse coordinates.
successCriteria: Two ref variables named x and y are created inside setup(), both initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created reactive state variables to track mouse position.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you create both x and y variables using ref(0).
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're creating two separate ref variables inside the setup() function, both initialized to 0.

steps.title: Define mouse move handler
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named handleMouseMove that takes an event parameter and updates the x and y ref values with the event's clientX and clientY coordinates.
steps.hint: The event object has clientX and clientY properties that give the mouse position relative to the viewport. Update the ref values by assigning to their .value property.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleMouseMove function is defined that updates the x and y refs when called with a mouse event.
successCriteria: The handleMouseMove function is defined, takes an event parameter, and updates both x.value and y.value with event.clientX and event.clientY.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the mouse movement handler that will track cursor coordinates.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function updates both x and y values using event.clientX and event.clientY.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler function isn't quite right. Check that you're defining a function named handleMouseMove that updates both x.value and y.value with the event coordinates.

steps.title: Add template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template section to your component with a div element that will track mouse movements.
steps.hint: In Vue single-file components, the template goes in a <template> tag. Add a <template> section above your script and include a div inside it.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding a template section
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a template section with a div element that will serve as the mouse tracking area.
successCriteria: The component includes a <template> section with a div element inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the template structure with a div element that will track mouse movements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both the <template> tag and a div element inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't quite right. Remember to add a <template> section with a div element inside it.

steps.title: Wire mouse event to handler
steps.instruction: In the template, add the @mousemove event listener to the div element and bind it to your handleMouseMove function.
steps.hint: Use Vue's @mousemove directive on the div element and set it equal to your handler function name.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding an event listener to an element
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The div element now has an @mousemove event listener that will trigger the handleMouseMove function when the mouse moves over it.
successCriteria: The div element has @mousemove="handleMouseMove" attribute added to it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully wired the mouse movement event to your handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added @mousemove="handleMouseMove" to the div element in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The div element doesn't have the mouse event listener properly set up. Add @mousemove="handleMouseMove" to the div element.

steps.title: Add render prop slot
steps.instruction: Add a <slot> element inside your template that exposes the x and y values as slot props.
steps.hint: In Vue, render props are implemented using scoped slots. The slot element can receive props that will be available to its content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a <slot> element that will allow parent components to access the mouse position data.
successCriteria: A <slot> element is added to the template with slot props exposing x and y values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the scoped slot that will enable the render props pattern.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a slot, but make sure it exposes both x and y as slot props.
steps.feedbackWrong: The slot element with proper slot props is missing. Remember to expose x and y values.

steps.title: Create DisplayMouse component
steps.instruction: Create a new Vue component named DisplayMouse that will display the mouse position. Define it with a template that shows the x and y coordinates.
steps.hint: You can create a new component using defineComponent and a template with placeholders for x and y values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DisplayMouse component is defined with a template that will eventually show mouse coordinates.
successCriteria: DisplayMouse component is created with defineComponent and has a template containing x and y placeholders.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the DisplayMouse component that will consume the mouse position data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it's named DisplayMouse and has a template with x/y placeholders.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DisplayMouse component wasn't properly created. Check that you used defineComponent and included a template.

steps.title: Use MouseTracker in DisplayMouse
steps.instruction: Inside the DisplayMouse component's template, use the MouseTracker component with a scoped slot to access the mouse position data.
steps.hint: Wrap your content with the MouseTracker component and use v-slot to receive the mouse coordinates.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: Using a component with scoped slot
steps.expectedOutcome: The DisplayMouse component will be able to consume mouse position data from MouseTracker via the render props pattern.
successCriteria: DisplayMouse component template contains MouseTracker with a scoped slot that receives mouse coordinates.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the render props pattern by using MouseTracker with a scoped slot in DisplayMouse.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the scoped slot syntax (v-slot) to access the mouse position data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DisplayMouse component should use MouseTracker with a scoped slot to receive mouse coordinates. Check the syntax for scoped slots in Vue.

steps.title: Display mouse coordinates
steps.instruction: Inside the DisplayMouse component's template, display the x and y coordinates from the slot props.
steps.hint: Access the slot props in the template using the variable name you defined when using the MouseTracker component.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying props in a template
steps.expectedOutcome: The mouse coordinates will be visible in the UI when moving the mouse over the tracking area.
successCriteria: The DisplayMouse component template shows the x and y coordinates from the slot props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You're successfully displaying the mouse coordinates using render props.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're accessing the slot props correctly in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The coordinates aren't displaying correctly. Check that you're using the correct prop names in the template.
